newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Bank of Albania raises shortterm lek deposit rates. [Corrected 19:53 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Bank of Albania raises shortterm lek deposit rates. [Corrected 19:53 gmt]

text.p: The Bank of Albania has lifted its short-term interest rates for lek deposits, the Albanian Central Bank (corrects from "state television") said on Friday.

It said 12-month deposits would yield 23 percent (corrects from "22 percent") against a previous 19 percent, six-month deposits would yield 21 percent against 18 percent (corrects from "18.5 percent) and three-month deposits would yield 21 percent (corrects from "20.5 percent") against 18.5 percent.
The changes will come into force on February 3, it said.
No-one was available for comment at the central bank. Official announcements are often made through state television.
The television said the Bank of Albania would intervene at appropriate moments to maintain macro-economic stability.
The lek has lost some 30 percent of its value against the U.S. dollar since the start of the year following the collapse of hugely popular pyramid investment schemes.
